transformer: The network design inside modern language models: dozens of stacked layers, each one attention followed by ordinary neurons.
large language model: A very big transformer trained on text to predict the next token. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini are built on them.
LLM: Short for large language model: a very big network trained on text to predict the next token.
pre-training: The first and biggest stage of training a language model: predicting the next token across an enormous pile of text.
base model: A language model straight out of pre-training. It continues documents and has not yet been taught to act as an assistant.
fine-tuning: Training an already-trained model some more on a smaller, special set of examples to change how it behaves.
RLHF: Reinforcement learning from human feedback: people compare answers, and the model is nudged toward the kind they prefer.
system prompt: Instructions placed at the top of the context window by whoever built the app. They set the assistant's role and rules, and the user usually cannot see them.
sampling: Choosing the next token at random, with likelier tokens chosen more often, instead of always taking the top one.
logit: A raw score a network gives to one possible answer, before softmax turns the scores into probabilities.
temperature: A sampling knob that divides every score before softmax. Low makes the favorite win almost every time; high evens out the odds.
top-k: A sampling knob: only the k highest-scoring tokens may be picked, and the rest are cut.
top-p: A sampling knob: keep the likeliest tokens until their probabilities add up to p, and cut the rest. Also called nucleus sampling.
